# Business Refinement — REQ-0001

Source revision: c94b223731ca60b9267799c1adc2238a29d69b404cb8cc9349bc653a04fcc7d6

## Confirmed information

### Business purpose and users

- **B-001** [D-0001] Littlelist users can attach an optional due date to a personal task, see that date in the task list and manage it during editing; tasks without due dates remain supported.

### Feature scope and existing product compatibility

- **B-002** [D-0002] Due dates are optional. A user can assign one during task creation or editing, display it clearly in the list, and subsequently change or remove it.
- **B-003** [D-0003] Preserve existing tasks without due dates and all existing CRUD and completion/reopening behavior.
- **B-004** [D-0004] Due dates persist across application restarts alongside existing task data.
- **B-005** [D-0005] Provide an intuitive, visually polished experience consistent with Littlelist.
- **B-006** [D-0006] Keep the change scoped to the local single-user demonstrator.

### Date eligibility and interpretation

- **B-007** [D-0007, D-0009, D-0010] Permit any valid calendar date, including past dates, today and future dates. Due dates remain optional; never reject a valid date merely because it is in the past.
- **B-008** [D-0012, D-0017, D-0020] Treat due dates as calendar dates in the device's local calendar, without timezone-related date shifts. Reject invalid calendar dates without overwriting the last valid saved value.

### Overdue presentation and completion

- **B-009** [D-0011, D-0016, D-0020] An unfinished task whose due date is before device-local today displays an explicit "Overdue" label with subtle warning styling. A task due today is not overdue. Preserve existing task ordering.
- **B-010** [D-0013, D-0018, D-0020] Completing a task retains its due date but removes overdue emphasis. Reopening restores overdue indication when applicable.

### Editing and clearing

- **B-011** [D-0014, D-0019, D-0020] Due-date editing and clearing follow existing autosave behavior. Clearing removes the optional due date. Cancel discards only unsaved or invalid drafts; previously saved changes remain saved.

## Unresolved issues

None recorded.

## Unconfirmed proposals

None recorded.

# Functional Analysis — REQ-0001

Baseline: 76f0b3fbf7a093a9633e5ca10b3fc396174bde50e728c4d251ac02a03942250e
Approval: BD-0001
Handoff: 4d98af74-7793-4ab1-85b1-c822a7192d3e

## Functional requirements

### FR-001 — Optional due date and visible task date
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0002
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Allow task creation with or without an optional due date, assignment during editing, and clear display of the assigned calendar date in the task list.

### FR-002 — Edit and clear with existing autosave
Business sources: B-002, B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0019
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Allow changing or clearing an assigned due date through existing editing/autosave behavior. Cancel discards only unsaved or invalid drafts and never undoes already saved changes.

### FR-003 — Calendar date eligibility and validation
Business sources: B-007, B-008
Discovery evidence: D-0009, D-0017
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Accept past, present and future valid calendar dates. Use the device local calendar without timezone-related shifts. Reject invalid calendar dates while preserving the last valid saved date; absence of a date is valid.

### FR-004 — Overdue presentation without reordering
Business sources: B-009
Discovery evidence: D-0016
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: For an unfinished task with a date before device-local today, show an explicit Overdue label and subtle warning styling. Today, future dates and undated tasks are not overdue. Preserve existing ordering.

### FR-005 — Completion retains due dates
Business sources: B-010
Discovery evidence: D-0018
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Completing a task retains its date without overdue emphasis. Reopening restores overdue indication if the retained date is before device-local today.

### FR-006 — Durability and CRUD compatibility
Business sources: B-003, B-004
Discovery evidence: D-0003, D-0004
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Persist assigned, changed and cleared dates across restarts. Preserve existing undated records and CRUD/completion behavior.

### FR-007 — Consistent Littlelist experience
Business sources: B-005
Discovery evidence: D-0005
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Present date creation, editing, clearing, display and validation as an intuitive, visually polished part of the existing Littlelist experience.

## Use cases

### UC-001 — Create task with optional date
Business sources: B-002, B-007, B-008, B-004, B-005
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0009, D-0017, D-0004, D-0005
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001, FR-003, FR-006, FR-007
Questions: -
Actor: Littlelist user
Preconditions: Littlelist is running and the user is creating a task.
Trigger: The user creates a task.
Main flow: 1. The user enters a valid task title and optionally selects a calendar date.
  2. The application validates the date when supplied.
  3. The application saves the task and shows its assigned date in the list.
Alternative flows: Leaving the date empty is valid. A past date is valid. An impossible date is rejected without being saved; existing task validation remains intact.
Outcome: The task and any selected date are available in the list and remain saved across restart.

### UC-002 — Edit, validate or clear a due date
Business sources: B-002, B-011, B-008, B-004, B-005
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0019, D-0017, D-0004, D-0005
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002, FR-003, FR-006, FR-007
Questions: -
Actor: Littlelist user
Preconditions: An existing task is available for editing.
Trigger: The user edits its due date.
Main flow: 1. The user opens the existing task editor.
  2. The user selects another date or clears the date.
  3. Valid changes follow existing autosave and update the task list.
Alternative flows: An invalid draft preserves the last valid saved date. Cancel discards only unsaved or invalid draft changes; previously autosaved changes remain saved.
Outcome: The valid new date or absence of date is saved; cancellation does not undo saved changes.

### UC-003 — View overdue state and complete or reopen
Business sources: B-002, B-009, B-010
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0016, D-0018
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001, FR-004, FR-005
Questions: -
Actor: Littlelist user
Preconditions: Tasks are available in the list, with or without dates.
Trigger: The user views tasks or changes completion state.
Main flow: 1. The application shows assigned dates and identifies unfinished tasks dated before local today as Overdue.
  2. The user completes a task; the date remains and overdue emphasis disappears.
  3. The user reopens it; overdue indication returns when applicable.
Alternative flows: Today and future dates do not cause overdue status. Undated tasks remain supported. Existing ordering does not change.
Outcome: Dates and completion-related presentation reflect the current task state without changing ordering.

## Business rules

### BR-001 — No chronological rejection
Business sources: B-007
Discovery evidence: D-0009
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-003
Questions: -
Statement: A valid calendar date must not be rejected solely because it is before today; due dates are optional.

### BR-002 — Overdue predicate
Business sources: B-009, B-010
Discovery evidence: D-0016, D-0018
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-004, FR-005
Questions: -
Statement: Overdue emphasis applies only to unfinished tasks with a due date strictly before device-local today; completed or undated tasks receive no overdue emphasis.

### BR-003 — Cancel is not rollback of saved changes
Business sources: B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0019
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Statement: Cancellation discards only the current unsaved or invalid draft; it does not revert earlier autosaved date changes.

## Acceptance criteria

### AC-001 — Create without a due date
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0002
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001
Questions: -
Given: A user is creating a task with a valid title.
When: The user leaves the due date empty and creates the task.
Then: The task is saved without a due date and remains usable.

### AC-002 — Past, today and future dates are accepted
Business sources: B-002, B-007, B-008
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0009, D-0017
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001, FR-003
Questions: -
Given: A user creates or edits a task and supplies a valid calendar date before, on or after device-local today.
When: The task or date change is saved.
Then: The selected date is accepted in all three cases; being past is never itself a rejection reason.

### AC-003 — Assigned date visible in task list
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0002
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001
Questions: -
Given: A task has a saved due date.
When: The user views the task list.
Then: The assigned calendar date is clearly visible for that task.

### AC-004 — Change an existing date
Business sources: B-002, B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0019
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Given: An existing task has a saved due date.
When: The user selects another valid date and existing autosave completes.
Then: The new date replaces the old date and is shown in the list.

### AC-005 — Clear an existing date
Business sources: B-002, B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0019
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Given: A task has a saved due date.
When: The user clears it and existing autosave completes.
Then: The date is removed; the task remains usable without a date and has no overdue indication.

### AC-006 — Invalid calendar draft preserves saved value
Business sources: B-008
Discovery evidence: D-0017
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-003
Questions: -
Given: A task has a last valid saved due date.
When: The user attempts to save an impossible calendar date.
Then: The invalid date is rejected and the last valid saved date remains unchanged.

### AC-007 — No timezone-related date shift
Business sources: B-008
Discovery evidence: D-0017
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-003
Questions: -
Given: A user selects a calendar date on a device with a local timezone different from UTC.
When: The date is saved and the task is viewed or reopened after restart.
Then: The same selected calendar date is displayed without shifting it through timezone conversion.

### AC-008 — Past unfinished task is overdue
Business sources: B-009
Discovery evidence: D-0016
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-004
Questions: -
Given: An unfinished task has a due date earlier than device-local today.
When: The user views the task list.
Then: The task shows an explicit Overdue label and subtle warning styling without changing task ordering.

### AC-009 — Today, future and undated tasks are not overdue
Business sources: B-009
Discovery evidence: D-0016
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-004
Questions: -
Given: Unfinished tasks have dates equal to today, after today, or no due date.
When: The user views the task list.
Then: None of these tasks shows overdue emphasis; ordering remains unchanged.

### AC-010 — Complete and reopen a dated task
Business sources: B-010
Discovery evidence: D-0018
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-005
Questions: -
Given: An unfinished dated task is overdue.
When: The user completes it and later reopens it.
Then: Completion retains the date and removes overdue emphasis; reopening restores it if the date is still before local today.

### AC-011 — Cancel unsaved draft retains saved changes
Business sources: B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0019
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Given: A date change has already autosaved and the user then makes an unsaved or invalid date draft.
When: The user cancels the draft.
Then: Only that draft is discarded; the most recently autosaved date or saved cleared state remains.

### AC-012 — Dates and cleared state persist across restart
Business sources: B-004
Discovery evidence: D-0004
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-006
Questions: -
Given: Tasks include an assigned date, a changed date and a cleared date.
When: The application is stopped and restarted.
Then: Each saved date or cleared state is retained for its task.

### AC-013 — Existing undated task compatibility
Business sources: B-003
Discovery evidence: D-0003
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-006
Questions: -
Given: Existing task data was created by the original CRUD application with no due-date fields.
When: The extended application opens that data.
Then: Existing titles, descriptions and completion states remain intact and the tasks have no due date.

### AC-014 — Original CRUD and completion regression
Business sources: B-003
Discovery evidence: D-0003
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-006
Questions: -
Given: Existing tasks and newly created tasks include dated and undated examples.
When: The user creates, reads, edits, completes, reopens and confirms deletion of tasks.
Then: The existing CRUD/completion behavior remains operational, including title validation and deletion confirmation.

### AC-015 — Consistent usable date controls
Business sources: B-005
Discovery evidence: D-0005
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-007
Questions: -
Given: The user operates Littlelist in its existing desktop or phone layout.
When: The user creates or edits a date and views its display and validation state.
Then: Date controls and messages remain readable and usable, visually consistent with the existing Littlelist layout.

## Business coverage

- **B-001** [contextual] - | Purpose and users; concrete behavior is elaborated by B-002.

- **B-002** [elaborated] FR-001, FR-002 | Optional dates, task-list display, changes and clearing.

- **B-003** [elaborated] FR-006 | Retain undated records and existing CRUD/completion.

- **B-004** [elaborated] FR-006 | Durable assigned, changed and cleared dates.

- **B-005** [elaborated] FR-007 | Consistent usable Littlelist experience.

- **B-006** [contextual] - | Local single-user demonstration boundary, not a new account/platform feature.

- **B-007** [elaborated] FR-003 | Any valid calendar date is permitted.

- **B-008** [elaborated] FR-003 | Local calendar interpretation and invalid-date preservation.

- **B-009** [elaborated] FR-004 | Overdue predicate, visible label and unchanged order.

- **B-010** [elaborated] FR-005 | Date retention across completion and reopening.

- **B-011** [elaborated] FR-002 | Autosave, clearing and cancel-draft behavior.

## Inherited unresolved items

None recorded.

## Analysis questions

None recorded.

## Analysis proposals

None recorded.

# Technical Design — REQ-0001

## Context and authority

AI-authored Technical Design for human review, not implementation authorization. Authority is approved Analysis baseline 63329d63c760e41f166e1b99d277534aeb8063e3469e7383a26e45ce4ad5e649 selected by explicit Analysis advancement faa97785-1068-4c72-9d78-e3683828ed05, retaining approved Business baseline 76f0b3fbf7a093a9633e5ca10b3fc396174bde50e728c4d251ac02a03942250e. Architecture 1.3.0 and Security 1.2.0 are the pinned contributors. QA strategy/scenarios already derive independently from Analysis; they do not authorize this design and are unchanged. All seven FRs and fifteen ACs are specified; no unresolved Business/Analysis items or exceptions exist.

Observed existing code: Node 25.9.0, built-in SQLite, a loopback-only JSON server and vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript with 450 ms edit autosave, prepared statements, required title, optional description, completion/reopening and confirmed deletion. Task DTO has id/title/description/completed, SQL has a private creation-order sequence, and schema user_version is 1. These observations inform the technical proposal; approved Analysis remains the business authority.

## Proposed solution

Retain the existing stack and module boundaries. Add no runtime dependency, external service, account system or new SDLC stage.

1. Add a small pure calendar-date helper usable by browser and Node validation, served through the existing fixed asset allowlist. It validates canonical date-only strings using calendar components/leap-year arithmetic, never timestamp parsing. Backend validation is authoritative; the browser provides immediate feedback. Absent dates are supported, with no comparison against today as an input-permission rule (FR-001/FR-003, AC-001/002/006/007).
2. Extend src/tasks.mjs DTO, validation, prepared CRUD statements and transactions with nullable dueDate. Add a transactional, additive SQLite v1-to-v2 migration that adds nullable due_date and preserves IDs, sequence, title, description and completion. Fresh databases use the same final schema. Recheck version under the migration lock; fail without replacing data on unsupported versions or migration failure. Date changes, clears and completion persist normally (FR-006, AC-012/013/014).
3. Extend the existing creation form and edit dialog with a labelled optional native calendar control, plus an explicit accessible clear action. Do not set min=today or any product date-window restriction. Use the platform calendar picker with readable saved date text, retain the existing visual language and phone/desktop responsiveness (FR-001/002/007, AC-001 through AC-005 and AC-015).
4. Extend draft/saved editor state and dirty checking to include dueDate. A valid change uses the existing 450 ms autosave. Detect native validity.badInput and incomplete/invalid drafts before converting an empty field to null. An explicit clear or genuinely empty valid field means absence; an invalid draft must never become a clearing PATCH. Keep last valid saved data until a valid save succeeds. Cancel stops unsaved work and keeps prior autosaves; while a save is in flight retain the current protective controls and serialize subsequent edits (FR-002/003, AC-004/005/006/011).
5. Render a date label as text on dated rows. Derive today from browser-local year/month/day, compare calendar tuples without converting the saved date to UTC, and set Overdue text plus subtle warning style only for incomplete tasks strictly before today. Compute again when rendering, on returning to the visible page and at the next local day boundary while open; date retention and existing creation-order sorting remain unchanged (FR-004/005, AC-008/009/010). Clock scheduling is a technical means to keep the confirmed rule current, not a new time-of-day requirement.
6. Preserve original CRUD behavior and failure handling. Unit/build checks stay with Engineering. QA may later bind the approved interface contract to separately reviewed automation; existing QA scenarios remain independent. No coding, dependency setup or tests are executed by this design draft.

## Security considerations

Security-by-design contribution, not a completed Security Review or certification. Assets are local task content, SQLite integrity and preserved evidence. Boundaries are browser input to JSON API, API to SQLite and the local filesystem. A malicious local page, malformed payload, invalid calendar or script-looking string must not corrupt data or execute markup.

Retain the fixed loopback binding, trusted Host/Origin checks, JSON-only requests, UTF-8/body-size handling, fixed static asset allowlist, CSP, no-store and prepared SQL. Serve the pure calendar helper only by an explicit allowlist entry, not directory traversal. Render task/date/error strings with textContent. Do not expose the database, local profile, runtime or SDLC evidence through HTTP. Validate dates before any mutation; failed PATCHes preserve saved data. Existing title/description and transport constraints are unchanged.

Threats/verification: reject malformed types/arrays/objects and impossible dates; exercise hostile text rendering and foreign-origin mutation protections; check failed edits and migration rollback on disposable copies. Preserve existing future-schema fail-closed handling. Do not impose past-date rejection, a UTC reference day, silent clearing, date sorting or restrictions on completed-date editing as a security shortcut; each would require business authority. No new authentication, external telemetry, credential storage or generic security infrastructure is proposed. A trusted local machine remains the deployment boundary.

## Coverage and uncertainty

Every active FR/AC is designed below; structured disposition implemented means planned design coverage, not code or passing tests.

- FR-001 / AC-001/002/003: optional creation/edit assignment and clear list display.
- FR-002 / AC-004/005/011: editing, clearing, serialized autosave and cancellation of only unsaved/invalid draft state.
- FR-003 / AC-002/006/007: past/today/future acceptance; real-calendar validation and timezone-stable date-only values.
- FR-004 / AC-008/009: visible local-calendar overdue predicate, no overdue on today/future/undated tasks and unchanged ordering.
- FR-005 / AC-010: completion retains dates, removes warning emphasis and restores it on reopening when applicable.
- FR-006 / AC-012/013/014: additive migration, real restart persistence and regression of existing CRUD/completion.
- FR-007 / AC-015: cohesive date controls, labels, validation, responsive layout and keyboard/focus behavior consistent with the existing app.

No unresolved business questions, unconfirmed assumptions or blocked requirements remain. The proposed module layout, nullable wire representation and migration are technical choices presented for Design approval. Risks requiring verification are ambiguous native invalid input versus clearing, autosave races, local-midnight/timezone day shifts and migration data safety; none is waived. No performance budget or certification absent from Analysis is invented.

The semantic conformance review must trace every negative condition/default: impossible dates to AC-006, optional omission/clear to AC-001/005, no warning on today/completed/undated to AC-009/010, last-saved preservation to AC-006/011. A source-bound Code Review must reject a hidden min=today, UTC-based day comparison, overwritten invalid draft, lost legacy record or unsupported date-window restriction. Final Verification must use actual joined Engineering/QA evidence, not this design coverage.

## Prototype limitations

None proposed. The governed limitation list is explicitly empty. All approved product behavior remains in scope. Generic Design approval will not authorize later observable exceptions, runtime rejection of otherwise permitted input or narrower behavior. Any consequential new limitation needs separate explicit effect authorization through the existing governance mechanism, preferably resolving the business behavior upstream instead.

## Alternatives

<!-- Optional section; omit when not applicable. -->

Keep the existing Node/SQLite/vanilla UI rather than a new frontend framework, ORM or hosted service: the change is small and the current architecture already supports persistence and browser testing. Store a nullable date-only string rather than an epoch timestamp: the requirement is a calendar date and must not shift across timezones. Use the existing editor/autosave rather than a separate Save workflow: preserves confirmed behavior. Use native calendar entry plus explicit validation/clear handling instead of a custom calendar dependency; browser-specific entry behavior must be checked through real UI tests. A third-party date library is unnecessary for this focused calendar operation; no dependency-security claim is inferred.

## Interfaces and data

<!-- Optional section; omit when not applicable. -->

Proposed task JSON becomes {id, title, description, completed, dueDate}, where dueDate is null or a canonical date-only string (for example 2026-10-29). No createdAt, due time, timezone identifier or overdue flag is persisted. The browser computes overdue using its own local calendar. This is an additive field; clients omitting it keep the existing create/update behavior.

- POST /api/tasks: missing dueDate or null creates an undated task; a valid calendar-date string assigns it. Existing title/description requirements remain.
- PATCH /api/tasks/:id: omitted dueDate preserves it, null clears it, a valid string replaces it. Empty strings, wrong types, date-time values, malformed/impossible calendar values are representation/validity errors, not past-date errors. UI maps an intentional valid empty/clear state to null.
- GET collection/item: return dueDate for each task, including null on legacy/undated records. No endpoint change. DELETE/completion behavior is retained; a completion-only PATCH does not change the date.
- Invalid date: HTTP 400 with the existing JSON error envelope, a stable INVALID_DUE_DATE code, field dueDate and a human-readable correction message; no write. Existing title and transport diagnostic behavior remains intact.
- Calendar representation uses zero-padded numeric year-month-day, with year represented by at least four digits. Use component validation and arithmetic for calendar validity; do not introduce a fixed four-digit-year maximum, rolling date window, epoch-range restriction, min=today, or UTC conversion. Calendar formatting and comparisons must not silently narrow the accepted date-only domain. Any platform input limitation must be surfaced for review rather than relabelled a business rule.
- SQLite v2 adds nullable due_date TEXT. v1 rows receive NULL without rewriting business data or the private sequence. Migration and user_version update commit together; a failure rolls back. Repeated startup is idempotent. Older baseline application binaries should not be used against v2 databases; retain an offline copy before a real migration if rollback is required. Development/QA must use disposable databases and never mutate archived evidence or personal data merely to test migration.
- Test seams: pure calendar validation/comparison/local-today helpers, store migration and CRUD, HTTP boundary, and real UI create/edit/clear/complete/cancel. Later QA automation owns qa/ paths and can use isolated legacy database fixtures plus controlled browser-local clocks/timezones. Avoid editing frozen BEFORE scripts/evidence to make new DTO assertions pass; update relevant active tests while preserving historical baseline fixtures/records.
- Before implementation/source-bound approval, finish and freeze supplemental presentation captures. Keep execution-generated output outside fingerprinted source or under reviewed Epic evidence paths. No new source exclusion is proposed. Engineering files stay outside qa/; this design does not modify the orchestrator.

It covers calendar/date-draft semantics, past/today/future validity, extended years, opposite local timezones, optional/edit/clear date persistence, completion retention, invalid-write preservation, additive legacy migration, migration rollback, repeated startup and original CRUD/store regressions.
